u1-01.title: One stone in the middle
u1-01.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black stone have?
u1-01.hint: Count only the empty points touching the stone along a board line.
u1-01.explanation: The four neighbouring intersections—up, down, left and right—are empty, so this stone has four liberties.

u1-02.title: One stone on the edge
u1-02.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black stone have?
u1-02.hint: The area outside the board cannot be counted.
u1-02.explanation: The black stone has three adjacent empty intersections: left, right and below.

u1-03.title: One stone in the corner
u1-03.prompt: How many liberties does the marked black stone have?
u1-03.hint: A corner has only two board lines leading inward.
u1-03.explanation: Only the points to the right and below are liberties, so the stone has two.

u1-04.title: Two connected stones
u1-04.prompt: How many liberties does this connected black group have?
u1-04.hint: The intersection between the stones is occupied, so it is not a liberty.
u1-04.explanation: Both stones form one group. Count the six different empty intersections around that group.

u1-05.title: Does a diagonal count?
u1-05.prompt: Do the two marked black stones already form one connected group?
u1-05.hint: Stones connect along horizontal or vertical board lines, not across a diagonal.
u1-05.explanation: The stones touch only diagonally. They are still two separate groups.

u1-06.title: Capture in the middle
u1-06.prompt: Black to play. Capture the marked white stone by taking its last liberty.
u1-06.hint: Look for the empty point directly next to White that is not occupied by Black.
u1-06.explanation: Black fills White's final liberty. With no liberties left, the white stone is captured.

u1-07.title: Capture at the edge
u1-07.prompt: Black to play. Find White's last liberty and capture the stone.
u1-07.hint: The board edge gives White no extra liberty. Check the point below it.
u1-07.explanation: The last liberty of this edge stone is directly below it; Black captures there.

u1-08.title: Capture in the corner
u1-08.prompt: Black to play. Capture the white stone in the corner.
u1-08.hint: A corner stone can only gain liberties at the two neighbouring intersections on the board.
u1-08.explanation: The point to the right is occupied by Black. The remaining liberty is below White.

u1-09.title: Capture two stones together
u1-09.prompt: Black to play. Capture the marked pair of connected white stones in one move.
u1-09.hint: Count the empty points around both white stones as one group.
u1-09.explanation: The two white stones share their liberties. Filling the last empty point below the left-hand stone captures the whole group.

u1-10.title: Save a stone in atari
u1-10.prompt: Black to play. Extend the marked black stone to escape atari.
u1-10.hint: The black stone has one liberty left. Check how many liberties the group would have after extending.
u1-10.explanation: Extending downward connects two black stones into one group with more liberties.

u2-01.title: Side-by-side stones
u2-01.prompt: Are the two marked black stones in the same connected group?
u2-01.hint: Follow the horizontal board line between them.
u2-01.explanation: The black stones touch directly along a horizontal line, so they belong to one group.

u2-02.title: Stones above and below
u2-02.prompt: Are the two marked white stones in the same connected group?
u2-02.hint: Follow the vertical board line between them.
u2-02.explanation: The white stones touch directly along a vertical line, so they form one group.

u2-03.title: Diagonal stones remain separate
u2-03.prompt: Are the two marked black stones already one connected group?
u2-03.hint: A diagonal contact is not a direct connection along a board line.
u2-03.explanation: Although they look close, the two stones are still separate groups.

u2-04.title: An opposing stone between them
u2-04.prompt: Are the two marked black stones part of one connected group?
u2-04.hint: Check what occupies the intersection between the black stones.
u2-04.explanation: A white stone separates them. The marked black stones are not directly connected.

u2-05.title: Join across the middle
u2-05.prompt: Black to play. Connect the two marked black stones directly with one move.
u2-05.hint: Find the empty intersection that touches both black stones along the board lines.
u2-05.explanation: Black plays on the shared adjacent point, linking the two stones into one group.

u2-06.title: Join vertically
u2-06.prompt: Black to play. Connect the upper and lower black stones into one group.
u2-06.hint: Check the empty intersection between the two black stones.
u2-06.explanation: Black fills the middle point, making a vertical connection between the stones.

u2-07.title: Connect near the edge
u2-07.prompt: Black to play. Join the two black stones near the left edge.
u2-07.hint: Look for the empty point touching both black stones.
u2-07.explanation: Filling the shared point joins the two stones along the same row.

u2-08.title: A cutting point in the middle
u2-08.prompt: Black to play. Occupy the point where the two marked white stones could connect directly.
u2-08.hint: Find the empty point directly between the two white stones.
u2-08.explanation: Black occupies the middle point, preventing White from connecting there in one move.

u2-09.title: Stop a vertical connection
u2-09.prompt: Black to play. Prevent the upper and lower white stones from connecting directly through the middle.
u2-09.hint: Look for the empty intersection shared by both white stones.
u2-09.explanation: Black occupies that intersection, stopping this direct vertical connection.

u2-10.title: Find the connecting point near the edge
u2-10.prompt: Black to play. Which point would White need to connect the two marked stones directly? Occupy it.
u2-10.hint: Look along the straight line between the two white stones.
u2-10.explanation: Black occupies the point between them, so White cannot connect there in one move.

u4-m01.title: Find the first vital point
u4-m01.prompt: Black to play. Find the point that turns this three-point eye space into two separate real eyes.
u4-m01.hint: Compare the middle point with the two ends. Which move separates the remaining empty space?
u4-m01.explanation: Black plays in the middle, leaving one enclosed empty point on each side. This is the basic straight-three eye-space shape.

u4-m02.title: Rotate the same eye shape
u4-m02.prompt: Black to play. Where is the vital point when the three-point shape is vertical?
u4-m02.hint: Rotating the shape does not change which point divides it into two.
u4-m02.explanation: Black occupies the middle. The top and bottom empty points become separate real eyes.

u4-m03.title: Deny White two eyes
u4-m03.prompt: Black to play. White wants to make two eyes from this connected three-point space. Which vital point should Black take first?
u4-m03.hint: Think about what would happen if White occupied the central point first.
u4-m03.explanation: Black takes the centre so White cannot use that point to split its eye space. White's strongest follow-up still needs to be read.

u4-m04.title: Attack the rotated eye shape
u4-m04.prompt: Black to play. Find the point that prevents White from making two eyes in the vertical shape.
u4-m04.hint: Find the middle of the three connected empty intersections.
u4-m04.explanation: Taking the middle denies White this two-eye formation. The task checks the first vital point, not every later killing variation.

u4-m05.title: Complete a second eye horizontally
u4-m05.prompt: Black to play. The left eye is already enclosed. Fill the missing boundary point of the second eye.
u4-m05.hint: Inspect the four neighbouring points around the right-hand empty eye space.
u4-m05.explanation: Black closes the missing boundary. Both separate empty points become enclosed real eyes.

u4-m06.title: Complete a second eye vertically
u4-m06.prompt: Black to play. Close the missing boundary point of the second eye in this rotated shape.
u4-m06.hint: Confirm the existing eye, then inspect which side of the other eye remains open.
u4-m06.explanation: Filling the gap leaves two separate enclosed eye points. The orientation does not change the condition.

u4-m07.title: Block White's second eye
u4-m07.prompt: Black to play. White is one move away from making a second eye. Occupy the missing boundary point first.
u4-m07.hint: Do not fill the already complete eye. Find the gap around the other candidate eye.
u4-m07.explanation: Black enters the outer gap, so the second empty point touches an opposing stone and is no longer a real white eye.

u4-m08.title: Block the rotated second eye
u4-m08.prompt: Black to play. Occupy the gap in White's second-eye boundary before White can close it.
u4-m08.hint: Compare both candidate eye points. One still has an unclosed boundary.
u4-m08.explanation: Black takes the gap, leaving White with only its existing eye in this task. This alone does not prove the entire group will die.

u3-01.title: A move with no liberties
u3-01.prompt: Black plays a stone that would have no liberties after the move, and no white stones are captured. Is that legal?
options: Yes, any point can be played first
No, it is an illegal self-capture
u3-01.hint: Imagine the liberties of Black's group after the move.
u3-01.explanation: A move that leaves your group with no liberties and captures nothing is illegal under these rules.

u3-02.title: Capturing removes the problem
u3-02.prompt: Black plays into a surrounded point but captures neighbouring white stones. How should the move be judged?
options: Legal if Black has liberties after the capture
Illegal because the point appeared surrounded
u3-02.hint: When you play, remove captured stones before counting your group's remaining liberties.
u3-02.explanation: The captured white stones are removed first. If Black then has liberties, this move is legal.

u3-03.title: Why does ko exist?
u3-03.prompt: Why does the simple ko rule prevent immediate recapture?
options: To prevent a repeating position from continuing forever
u3-03.hint: What would happen if each player captured back on every turn?
u3-03.explanation: The ko rule prevents two players from repeating the same board position indefinitely.

u3-04.title: After a ko capture
u3-04.prompt: White has just captured a black stone in a simple ko. What may Black do next?
u3-04.hint: Simple ko forbids the immediate move that recreates the previous position.
u3-04.explanation: Black cannot recapture immediately. Black must play elsewhere first.

u3-05.title: What is a ko threat?
u3-05.prompt: Black plays elsewhere and creates a threat White may have to answer before Black fights for the ko again. What is that move called?
u3-05.hint: This threat creates a reason for the opponent to respond before the ko fight continues.
u3-05.explanation: A move that pressures the opponent to answer while fighting a ko is called a ko threat.

u3-06.title: Which ko rule does this app use?
u3-06.prompt: Which repetition restriction does the current interactive rules engine enforce?
options: Simple ko: no immediate return to the preceding board position
Superko: no repetition of any earlier position
u3-06.hint: The lessons use the common beginner version that looks one board position back.
u3-06.explanation: This engine implements simple ko and prevents an immediate return to the previous board position.
